doc: SCHEMA.md's ORDER token, applied end to end: a query in, the ids in the order it leaves them. `sort:COL' and `sort:COL:desc' name one column each, `sort:A->B' chains them in one token and is exactly the tokens said once, written order is precedence, and the token narrows NOTHING -- so every case here asserts an order over the same four rows unless a predicate is spelled beside it. The view declares `title' ascending, which is the order a query naming no sort key leaves standing and the answer every refusal falls back to. A sort token names one column in one direction: a negation, an alternation, a column no view carries and a direction that is neither word are each a query a producer answers as an error, and a renderer, having nobody to refuse to, drops the key -- so the rows come back in the declared order, unnarrowed. A column named twice is NO error on either side: the first spelling stands and the later one is dropped. The `*none*' cases take the `arrival' view instead, whose rows arrive in an order the declared sort does not put them in -- which is the only way to tell the EMPTY chain from the declared one. Browser-renderer only, like the other query vectors: table-view.el has no query grammar.

cases.name: no sort token leaves the declared order standing
a sort token states the order
rows equal on the key keep the order they arrived in
cases.doc: `c' and `d' both score 20 and the store lists c first; the sort is stable on both renderers.

cases.name: `:desc' takes the other direction
`:asc' spells the direction it already had
and a trailing colon is a direction half typed, which ascends
cases.doc: The token is committed as the reader passes through it toward `:desc'; an unspelled direction is the default one.

cases.name: written order is precedence
cases.doc: A badge column orders by its palette, so TODO leads DONE and the score settles each group.

cases.name: and reversing the tokens reverses the precedence
a column named twice keeps the first spelling
cases.doc: A chain never names a column twice, so the rule over the tokens that spell one is that the first stands and the later one is dropped. No error on either side.

cases.name: and the other way round, so it is the FIRST spelling that rules rather than a direction
two spellings of ONE direction are one ordering
cases.doc: `:asc' spells what an unspelled direction already means, so this repeat changes nothing at all -- which is what makes collapsing the twin safe.

cases.name: a repeat does not move the column's place in the chain
cases.doc: `state' leads because it was written first; the trailing spelling neither demotes it nor flips it. Last-wins would read DONE before TODO.

cases.name: `->' chains one token's columns, and it is the tokens said once
cases.doc: SUGAR, and one semantics: a token's segments are read as exactly the tokens they compose. Every case in this block pairs with one above it and asserts the same order.

cases.name: and written order inside the token is the same precedence
a segment carries its own direction
cases.doc: `sort:state sort:score:desc' said once: the departments keep their palette order and the tie-breaker reverses inside them.

cases.name: the two spellings mix, and precedence reads straight through
first-wins dedup spans the segments of one token
and spans the boundary between a segment and a token
whichever side of the arrow the twin falls on
a trailing arrow is a segment half typed, which is the `key:' rule
cases.doc: `sort:score sort:'. It is the state a reader passes through on the way to the next column, so it has to mean what it will mean.

cases.name: and a leading one is that same nothing ahead of the chain
a refusal is the SEGMENT's, and the rest of the chain stands
cases.doc: `sort:score sort:nope': a producer refuses the query and names the token, a renderer drops the key. The segments beside it order as written either way.

cases.name: wherever in the chain it falls
a direction that is neither word drops its own segment
an alternation drops its own segment too
a negation covers the WHOLE token, every segment of it
cases.doc: The `-' is written before the key, so there is no segment it does not reach: nothing is ordered and the declared order stands.

cases.name: `sortable' gates the gesture rather than the token, here too
and a chain narrows nothing, like every other sort token
empty cells settle at one end, outside the direction
and reversing the key does not drag them along
`sortable' gates the reader's gesture, never the token
cases.doc: `title' opts out of sorting and a chain naming it still opens as written, the way a declared `sort' does.

cases.name: a sort token narrows nothing
a predicate narrows what the token orders
free text narrows beside it the same way
cases.doc: Every title holds an `a', so the set is the set and the order is the token's.

cases.name: and a meta is a value like any other beside one
a negation orders nothing and narrows nothing
an alternation orders nothing and narrows nothing
a column no view carries orders nothing and narrows nothing
a direction that is neither word orders nothing and narrows nothing
a half-typed sort key is the `key:' rule
a refused token still narrows nothing beside a good one
cases.doc: The good key orders; the refused one is dropped rather than emptying the table.

cases.name: and an exact repeat is the position the key already holds
cases.doc: Idempotent, like every other token under the one combination rule -- which is what lets a consumer collapse the twin without changing what was asked.

cases.name: the `arrival' view is stated in an order its declared sort does not put it in
cases.doc: The rows arrive d, b, a, c and the view declares `title' ascending, so the declared order is a, b, c, d. Every `*none*' case below turns on those two being different.

cases.name: `sort:*none*' is the EMPTY chain, and the rows are read in the order they arrived
so it REPLACES the declared order rather than falling back to it
cases.doc: It names a sort key, and a query naming any sort key replaces the declared `sort'. It is what a reader has instead of a token to take off.

cases.name: the stars are read: a bare `none' is a column name and no view carries it
and the value folds, like every other value
a key that RESOLVES outranks it, and the companion is the whole chain
cases.doc: The pair is a query a producer refuses; a renderer, having nobody to refuse to, drops the `*none*' and lets the companion stand. The producer is the stricter of the two and no row moves either way.

cases.name: wherever among the tokens it is written
a REFUSED companion does not outrank it, having resolved to nothing
a negation of it is a refusal like any other, and the declared order stands
an alternation holding it is one too
and a direction on it is no token the grammar has
cases.doc: `*none*' names no column, so there is nothing for a direction to order; the token resolves to neither the meta nor a key and is dropped.

cases.name: spelling it twice is spelling it once
and twice inside one token is the same once
MID-CHAIN it is the companion rule said another way
cases.doc: `sort:score sort:*none*'. A producer refuses the pair naming the meta wherever it is written; a renderer lets the key that resolves outrank it, arrow or no arrow.

cases.name: and at the head of one, with the chain behind it
and it narrows nothing, like every other sort token
cases.doc: The predicate leaves two rows and the arrival order is what they are read in.
